defect.summary: op3's one-record quantum keys its contingency cells with a hand-rolled `${context}\u0001${outcome}` string and T20 then PARSED that key back into its parts. The delimiter is ASSUMED forbidden, not forbidden: a label containing U+0001 splits at the wrong place, so the parsed outcome matches no outcome and the parsed context matches no context, both `continue` guards stop firing, and each affected cell contributes four recomputes where the invariant says two.
defect.ground: CODEX, 2026-10-03, on T20 (f852cdf): a U+0001 context label gives 12 recomputes where the invariant says 8. REPRODUCED BY THIS SEAT at bytes, and wider than reported: a 2x2 table with all four cells occupied gives 8 with plain labels, 12 with one U+0001 in a context label, and 16 with U+0001 in both. The mechanism is fully accounted for - with the parse broken, `to === from` and `to === context` never match, so both loops try every label instead of every OTHER label, giving 4 per affected cell instead of 2 (two affected cells x 4, plus two clean cells x 2, equals 12). THE QUANTUM VALUE IS NOT AFFECTED: the extra moves are no-ops (a record relabelled to the label it already has), and a no-op cannot raise a maximum. What is wrong is the COUNT the invariant pins and the AXIS the move string names. AND THE HOUSE HAD ALREADY FIXED THIS ONCE, THREE WEEKS EARLIER: src/mica/tuple-key.ts exists because narrow-W, narrow-R and narrow-K had drifted onto three different assumed-forbidden delimiters, and its header says why in its own words - the safety 'rests entirely on NUL never appearing inside a component, which is a property of the INPUT, not of the encoding.' narrow-k's suite already asserts tupleKey(['a','bc']) !== tupleKey(['ab','c']). op3's quantum hand-rolled the same mistake anyway, and T20 made the latent ambiguity live. FINALLY, WHAT CURRENTLY DEFENDS THE LIVE BOX IS IN ANOTHER REPOSITORY: the caller's IDENT_PATTERN is /^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$/ (mica-service.ts:838), so no control character can reach these labels today. A core reader whose correctness rests on a regex in the bridge repo is exactly the cross-repo dependency this project forbids, and it is not a defence src/mica can see or test.

arbiter.word: I, the arbiter, grant T22: op3-node-response keys the cells of its quantum by the repository's shared collision-proof tuple key and never by an assumed-forbidden delimiter, so that two distinct labels can never share a cell and the count the invariant pins is the count the gate performs.

conditions: 1. The cell key is `tupleKey` from src/mica/tuple-key.ts - the house's shared, length-prefixed, collision-proof encoding - and NOT a second copy of the idea. One primitive, one source, every caller.

2. THE PARSE IS GONE. The map carries `context` and `outcome` beside the index, so nothing is encoded and then decoded. A key that must be parsed back into its parts is a second shape beside the first, which is the seam this project has paid for repeatedly.

3. A test sweeps EVERY C0 control character, U+0000 through U+001F, with the character placed in BOTH axes' labels, and asserts the recompute invariant `occupied * ((kO-1)+(kC-1))` holds for all 32 and that four distinct cells stay four. U+0001 was never special; it was only the delimiter that had been chosen.

4. A test uses a fixture whose two cells COLLIDE under the old encoding - (context 'A\u0001X', outcome 'Y') and (context 'A', outcome 'X\u0001Y') share a key - and asserts they remain two cells. ⛔ THIS CONDITION EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS TICKET'S OWN SUITE DID NOT CATCH THE BUG: a mutation restoring the ambiguous delimiter left 44/44 green, because the control-character sweep pins the PARSE and no fixture in it made two pairs COLLIDE. Found by the mutation differential, not by reading. The condition is therefore written as the property, not as the test.

5. THE TEST'S OWN COPY OF THE AMBIGUOUS ENCODING IS REPLACED TOO. `occupied` was computed in the suite with the same `${left}\u0001${right}` rule as the shipped code, so the expected value and the measured value were wrong together and agreed. On the existing fixtures they happened to agree correctly, which is how a latent bug survives a test.

6. No change to the quantum's VALUE, and it is asserted rather than assumed: the brute-force reference over both axes still agrees with the cheap form to twelve places on both shapes, and the containment property `broad >= narrow` still holds.
7. No new injected number, no new declaration field, no change to any blind reason code or verdict text. This repairs a count and a sentence, not a reading.
8. The 20 frozen scenarios in src/mica/verdict-logic.frozen.json stay BYTE-IDENTICAL, and src/mica/op-ceilings.test.ts does not move.

9. OPENS DERIVED BY THE SWEEP, NOT WRITTEN, AND THE PREDICTION HELD. opens-sweep --compare out/t20-cand-20261003T130018Z.tsv out/t22-derive-20261003T134430Z.tsv over two full declared-population arms (n=107 both sides): 99 of 103 comparable identical, 4 moved, 0 register-excluded, 4 printed no count line. DERIVED opens (2): src/mica/op3-node-response/index.ts and op3-node-response.test.ts - EXACTLY the two files T20 opened, which is what this ticket predicted before the sweep ran. The three other movers are each classified by the tool and none is this ticket's: core-door.test.ts 31/0 to 30/1 and glue.test.ts 136/0 to 135/1 are the DOOR OBJECTING to an uncommitted core edit with no live ticket, cleared by the repin; tools/ticket-preflight/preflight.test.ts 22 to 24 is commit fe90d74's, outside CORE_SCOPE. ⚠ AND THE BASE ARM IS ONE COMMIT OLD, WHICH IS WHY preflight.test.ts APPEARS AT ALL: the arm was captured at f852cdf and the tip is fe90d74. A tsv does not record the commit it was taken at, so --compare cannot detect that mismatch itself - the loose end logged to the board at 12:16Z, biting here in a small and fully explained way.

10. ⛔ THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS DERIVATION WAS REFUSED BY THE SWEEP'S OWN RULE, AND THE RULE WAS RIGHT. `--base fe90d74` resolves to HEAD, and the tool refused: "HEAD..HEAD is empty, so the EDITED half of the derivation would be silently empty and the `opens` list short." This repair is UNCOMMITTED, so there is no base to name: the edited half comes from `git status`, which is exactly the no---base path. The rule was built and shipped at 11:35Z today after this seat chose the wrong base twice; it caught its author at 13:5xZ. A rule a seat has to remember is a rule the next seat will not - and the next seat was me, two hours later.
